reel.linkedin: In January 1980, silver reached $49.45 per ounce after Nelson and William Herbert Hunt accumulated over 100 million ounces through futures and physical holdings. On March 27, 1980, Silver Thursday, their position collapsed and silver fell to $10.80 in a single session. The episode reshaped commodity regulation and produced the CFTC position limits still in place today. Full historical breakdown: https://fuseddistribution.com/blog/hunt-brothers-silver-squeeze/ Worth reading for anyone tracking silver markets.

photo.facebook: Silver hit $49.45 per ounce in January 1980. Not because of industrial demand or a currency crisis. Two brothers from Texas had been quietly accumulating 100 million ounces since 1973. Then the COMEX changed the rules and the whole position unwound in a day. That's Silver Thursday. The lessons for physical silver holders are still relevant. Do you think the silver market is still being manipulated today, or was the Hunt Brothers story a one-time event?
